scrim.note: Carbon ink at 28 % alpha; the dimming layer behind the narrow rail sheet only.

scrim-dark.note: Black at 50 % alpha; the dimming layer behind the narrow rail sheet only.

display.purpose: The greeting under the core and page titles; 24px when the window is 700px tall or less.

title.purpose: Section heads, artifact titles; 14px/600 for the column title and System heads, 13px/600 for code page panel heads.

body-reply.purpose: Assistant replies and documents; transcript at most 760px wide, documents 72ch.

label.purpose: Buttons, chips, tabs, tool card heads.

caption.purpose: Meta, snippets, tile subtitles, the Recents heading at 600.

mono-data.purpose: Numbers, paths, model ids, file types, diffs, readouts; 12 to 13px, tabular.

mono-figure.purpose: The three headline system readings; never wraps.

brand.purpose: JARVIS in the rail, beside the atom mark.

mono-symbol.purpose: The two-letter symbol on an element tile (artifact type).

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Menus, palette, floating panels, rail sheet, focused composer.

shadows.name: atom-teal
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow: the flat atom recipe (crescent and rim) on a teal disc; 1px / 1.25px on atoms of 10px or less.

shadows.name: atom-hollow
shadows.purpose: Pending reply or approval awaiting an answer (fill: ground); rod ring for system notes and unknown services.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus everywhere; rail search uses a rail-teal border instead.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow: the dimming layer behind the rail sheet under 1024px; a click on it closes the sheet.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default for every transition and entrance.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Hover and press colour, opacity and scale.

motion.name: mid
motion.purpose: Border/shadow changes, chevrons, atom tone changes.

motion.name: atom-in
motion.purpose: An atom arriving in the step chain.

motion.name: bond-in
motion.value: 320ms ease-out, 60ms delay, scaleY 0 to 1 from the top
motion.purpose: The bond drawing in after its atom.

motion.name: pop-in
motion.purpose: Menus, palette, chips, tabs, floating panels.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.purpose: User messages and tool cards. Not used on the empty page: there only the core moves.

motion.name: first-message
motion.value: core snapshot flies into the first reply's atom over 560ms (moves by 60%, then fades) while the live core fades in over the same span; composer slides to the foot over 420ms
motion.purpose: The moment the core becomes the first atom of a conversation: one object handed over (src/nodes/ui.js).

motion.name: core
motion.value: idle yaw 0.14 rad/s; swell (up to 16%), wobble and breath come only from the shared speech/thinking level (mesh-state.js), so an idle core holds its size; drag momentum decays at e^-2.2t; click knocks the 4 nearest atoms on a spring k=60 c=8

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all animation and transition durations 0.01ms; core: no spin, swell or breathe, drag still turns it; no first-message flight

motion.name: scrim
motion.purpose: The scrim behind the narrow rail sheet.

breakpoints.name: rail-sheet
breakpoints.purpose: Rail hidden by default, opens as a sheet over a scrim; scrim click or Escape closes it.

breakpoints.name: code-right
breakpoints.purpose: Code page hides the tasks and changes column.

breakpoints.name: composer-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Drop the token meter, then shorten the model name.

layout.core: 168px (120px short), 48 atoms, 3 neighbours; live core 26px, the same 48-atom cage with atoms drawn 1.8x

narrative.overview:
JARVIS's work is a structure being assembled in front of its owner. The ground is lab-white with a cool teal cast, the sidebar rail is carbon in both themes, JARVIS itself is teal plastic, and everything that connects one thing to another is a pale grey rod. The signature object is the core: a 48-atom ball-and-stick cage on a Fibonacci sphere that turns slowly, swells with streamed speech, breathes while thinking and spins when dragged. The kit also has a periodic table: each artifact type is an element tile with a two-letter symbol. The same vocabulary carries into the conversation: every reply, action and system note of a turn is an atom, and consecutive ones are bonded by a vertical rod into a step chain. Services at the foot of the rail are atoms on one horizontal bond.

The system is calm and dense in the way a desktop tool is dense: 14 px interface text, 15 px reading text, quiet 1 px lines, flat surfaces, one colour that means "JARVIS" and one that means "wrong". Depth comes from tone (ground, surface, sunk) rather than from shadows; only things that float over content cast one. Atoms are flat discs, never shaded spheres: a fill, a darker rim and a small white crescent on the upper left.

It rejects the grey chat column with a logo on top, and the cyan hologram on black that the old HUD used.
keyCharacteristics: Lab-white ground (light) or deep carbon-teal ground (dark); the rail is carbon in both.
One voice colour, teal, for JARVIS's atoms, the primary action, focus, the current item and the middle load level.
Red only for errors, denials and the high load level.
Flat atoms (fill, rim, crescent) and round-capped grey rods as the recurring motif.
Segoe UI Variable for text, Cascadia Code for every number, path, model id and element symbol.
Motion is "arrive and bond": a scale-in for the atom, a draw-in for its rod. On the empty page only the core moves by itself; greeting, starters and machine line are still.

rules.name: The One Plastic Rule
rules.body: Teal means JARVIS, the action you are about to take, or where you are. It never decorates a section, a heading or a chart series that carries no state.

rules.name: The Red Atom Rule
rules.body: Red is for something that went wrong or was refused, and for the high load level. A warning that is only "busy" is teal, not red.

rules.name: The Grey Rod Rule
rules.body: Bonds, idle bars and sparklines are grey. A bar or sparkline turns teal at the middle level and red at the high level; below that it stays grey.

rules.name: The Carbon Rail Rule
rules.body: The rail is carbon in light and dark alike and uses its own rail-* tokens; main-area tokens are never used on the rail.

rules.name: The Element Symbol Rule
rules.body: Every number, path, command, model id and element symbol is set in Cascadia Code with tabular figures; prose and controls never are. A type's readable word (Chart, Page, Document) is set in Segoe on the line under the title.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: All labels, headings and buttons are sentence case. No uppercase labels, no letter-spaced small caps. The JARVIS wordmark is the one name set in capitals.

rules.name: The Float Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is above the page": a menu, a sheet, a floating panel, the focused composer. Resting cards, tiles and tool steps have a border and no shadow.

rules.name: The Flat Atom Rule
rules.body: Atoms are fill, rim and crescent; never a radial gradient, a drop shadow or a glow.

rules.name: The Straight Bond Rule
rules.body: Outside the core, a bond is straight and axis-aligned: vertical between steps, horizontal between services.

dos: **Do** draw every atom with the flat recipe: fill, a 1.25 to 1.5 px inset rim in the darker shade, and a 1 to 1.5 px white crescent on the upper left (45 to 60 % white).
**Do** use teal-text, never teal, for teal text smaller than 18 px; keep teal for fills, rings, atoms and icons.
**Do** make every text colour reach 4.5:1 on ground, surface, sunk, sunk-2, bubble and teal-soft (and on rail, rail-hover and rail-active for rail text).
**Do** set numbers, paths, model ids and file types in Cascadia Code with tabular figures.
**Do** animate an arriving atom with a 280 ms ease-out scale from 0.4, and draw its bond in after it (320 ms, 60 ms later).

**Do** keep motion within 120 to 320 ms for state changes on the ease-out curve (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), and remove it entirely under reduced motion; the core then stops spinning and swelling but still turns when dragged.
**Do** hand the core over in one piece on the first message: its snapshot flies into the first reply's atom (560 ms) while the live core fades in over the same span.
**Do** use inline SVG line icons from the shared icon set, including the close mark at 14 px; never a text glyph.
**Do** draw an artifact's type as an element tile with its symbol from the shared helper, and keep the type word readable to screen readers.
donts: **Don't** use gradients anywhere, including radial shading on atoms or a ramp across the core; depth is stepped flat tones.
**Don't** add glow, coloured shadows or blur halos; the only shadows are the neutral rest and float shadows.
**Don't** colour a section, a heading or an idle chart: no per-section hues, no teal bars below the middle level.
**Don't** use green anywhere except the background of added diff lines.
**Don't** use uppercase labels or letter-spaced small caps; everything is sentence case.
**Don't** load web fonts; Segoe UI Variable and Cascadia Code are system faces.
**Don't** give resting cards, tiles or tool steps a shadow.
**Don't** box the System readings in tiles or fill a trace with an area; one hairline-divided row and a line are enough.
**Don't** describe the classic warm-grey interface (classic.html) as this system; it is a separate, frozen layout.
